key_terms: A set of equal-length Arrow columns sharing one schema, representing one batch of rows.
A column made of several contiguous array pieces. Chunk boundaries reflect storage or arrival history, not customer groups, file partitions or transactions.
A native, typed Arrow function such as filter, greater or sum that processes whole arrays instead of looping over Python values.
How a kernel treats missing inputs. A comparison with null yields null, and a filter must state whether a null selection drops the row or emits a null slot.
Replacing nulls with a stated value, as fill_null does, before computing, so the business choice about missing data is visible in the code.

worked_examples.title: Merge chunk means from sums and counts
worked_examples.code:
import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.compute as pc

values = pa.chunked_array([[4], [None, 8, 2, 6]], type=pa.int64())
naive = sum(pc.mean(chunk).as_py() for chunk in values.chunks) / values.num_chunks
sums = sum(pc.sum(chunk).as_py() for chunk in values.chunks)
counts = sum(len(chunk) - chunk.null_count for chunk in values.chunks)
print(naive, sums / counts, pc.mean(values).as_py())
worked_examples.interpretation: Averaging the two chunk means gives about 4.67, while merging sums and counts gives 5, matching the compute kernel on the whole chunked array. The naive version weights a one-row chunk the same as a four-row chunk. Any custom code that combines partial aggregates across chunks, files or partitions has the same trap, so test it with deliberately unequal chunk sizes.

worked_examples.title: Keep unknown filter results visible
worked_examples.code:
import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.compute as pc

values = pa.chunked_array([[4, None, 8], [2, 6]], type=pa.int64())
mask = pc.greater(values, 5)
print(pc.filter(values, mask).to_pylist())
print(pc.filter(values, mask, null_selection_behavior="emit_null").to_pylist())
worked_examples.interpretation: The default filter drops the null comparison result along with the false ones, leaving 8 and 6. With emit_null, the unknown row stays as a null so a reviewer can see that one measurement could not be classified. Use the second form when building exception reports, because silently dropping unknown rows makes a filtered count look more certain than the data allows.
